question: Does a fixed line sum, half-turn symmetry and one fixed entry uniquely determine a five-by-five magic square?
prior_information: Supplied discussion proposed uniqueness, then retracted it after noticing dependent constraints; later suggested dimensions five and fifteen for orders five and seven. These are prior claims, not predictions made blind.
model: All n*n cells are rational variables. Every row, column and both main diagonals have the same prescribed constant. Half-turn means x[r,c]=x[n-1-r,n-1-c]; transpose is a separate comparison model.
procedure: Build homogeneous difference constraints (all line sums zero) in row-major cell order.
Compute exact rational RREF, rank, free columns and a nullspace basis.
For half-turn models, add a zero change constraint at each individual cell in turn and recompute dimension.
Read LP1-05 converted values and LP1-16 decimal values from stored transcriptions. Verify their line sums and half-turn symmetry.

For each cell in each actual 5x5 grid, construct the first nonzero integral null vector keeping that cell fixed. Try plus then minus one primitive step; record whether the entire changed grid is positive. No random search.
criterion: Any two distinct positive integer grids with the same fixed line sum, half-turn symmetry and identical chosen cell disprove uniqueness under those constraints. Dimensions concern the rational affine solution space, not a count of positive integer grids.
exclusions: No primality restrictions on other cells
No requirement that entries be distinct or use 1..n*n
No claim of reproducing the historical submission validator
No inference about the author choosing particular primes
No claim that arbitrary rational free parameters always yield positive integers
Order seven is a mathematical comparison, not an audited historical 7x7 transcription
validation: Independently compare rank modulo two large primes; directly check each basis vector against row/column/diagonal and symmetry rules; verify every counterexample with direct arithmetic. Check known 3x3 cases.
